# Where Does the Prompt Go? Probing Prompt Adherence in Diffusion Models

*Generated by `report/build_report.py` from `README_template.md`; numbers come from the saved results.*

Hypothesis-driven study of how classifier-free guidance (CFG) scale and denoising steps affect compositional prompt
adherence (presence, attribute binding, counting, spatial relations, multiple constraints) in Stable Diffusion 1.5, whether
token-level cross-attention relates to success or failure, and whether a simple attention re-weighting helps. Hypotheses, mechanism and analysis plan: [report/protocol.md](report/protocol.md).
Results and discussion: [report/report.md](report/report.md). Evaluator validation: [report/validation.md](report/validation.md). Presentation material: `report/presentation.pptx`, [report/speaker_notes.md](report/speaker_notes.md), [report/defense.md](report/defense.md).

**Headline.** CFG 2 -> 7.5 raised image-text similarity ({clip72_diff}), lowered diversity ({div_2} to {div_7p5}) and localised object attention, but the rise in measured adherence ({cfg72_all_diff}, 95% CI {cfg72_all_ci}) is not statistically established;
more steps and CFG 15 gave no benefit; binding and multi-constraint prompts mostly fail at every setting. Attention re-weighting of object/colour tokens (matched prompts, seeds, CFG, steps; pre-registered) changed overall success by {intc_primary_all_rw2_vs_rw1} {intc_primary_all_rw2_vs_rw1_ci}:
**H4 not supported**; object presence improved as an exploratory lead. Main hypothesis: directionally consistent, **inconclusive**.

## Layout
```
configs/experiment.json     model id, CFG scales, step counts, seeds
data/prompts.json           28 prompts with structured constraints (built by src/build_benchmark.py)
data/validation_*.json      manual validation subset, final labels (and validation_subsets_images/ copies)
src/build_benchmark.py      template-based prompt generator
src/generate.py             Prompt x CFG x steps x seed generation (resumable) -> images + samples.jsonl
src/evaluate.py             OWL-ViT + CLIP scoring -> detections.jsonl, eval.jsonl
src/validate_metrics.py     evaluator vs manual labels
src/attention.py            cross-attention hook + extraction -> attention/*.npz
src/intervene.py            attention re-weighting intervention (control s=1, s=2, s=4)
src/analyze.py              statistics -> results/*.csv, tables.md
src/analyze_attention.py    attention summaries, AUCs -> results/attention_*.csv
src/analyze_intervention.py intervention vs control statistics -> outputs/intervention/results
src/report_numbers.py       collects every quoted number from the result files
src/figures.py              all figures -> figures/*.png
tests/                      unit tests (scoring, benchmark, token alignment) and a GPU attention test
report/                     protocol, validation, report (generated), defense (generated), slide builder
outputs/                    images, metadata, evaluation, attention maps, results, figures (not versioned)
```

## Requirements
Windows 11 (tested), Python 3.13 (3.14 has no PyTorch wheels), NVIDIA GPU with >= 6 GB VRAM and ~3.5 GB free (tested: RTX 3050 Laptop 6 GB), ~10 GB disk
for models + outputs. Models are downloaded from Hugging Face on first use into `models/`: `stable-diffusion-v1-5/stable-diffusion-v1-5` (fp16, ~2.1 GB, CreativeML OpenRAIL-M, not gated; a mirror of the deprecated runwayml repository),
`google/owlvit-base-patch32`, `openai/clip-vit-base-patch32`.

## Run
```powershell
.\.venv\Scripts\python -m pytest -q tests                                                  # {test_summary}
.\.venv\Scripts\python src\build_benchmark.py                                              # regenerates data/prompts.json
.\.venv\Scripts\python src\generate.py --out outputs\smoke --limit-prompts binding_cube_sphere_v1 --seeds 1   # smoke test: 6 images
.\.venv\Scripts\python src\generate.py --out outputs\main --seeds 2                        # pilot (336 images, ~40 min)
.\.venv\Scripts\python src\generate.py --out outputs\main                                  # main run (resumes; {n_images} images)
.\.venv\Scripts\python src\evaluate.py --run outputs\main                                  # detections + scores (--rescore to only rescore)
.\.venv\Scripts\python src\validate_metrics.py --run outputs\main
.\.venv\Scripts\python src\attention.py --run outputs\main --steps 40 --check 5            # {n_attention} images; --check = bit-identity test
.\.venv\Scripts\python src\analyze.py --run outputs\main
.\.venv\Scripts\python src\analyze_attention.py --run outputs\main
.\.venv\Scripts\python src\intervene.py --out outputs\intervention --scales 1 2 4          # {int_n_images} images, ~80 min
.\.venv\Scripts\python src\evaluate.py --run outputs\intervention
.\.venv\Scripts\python src\analyze_intervention.py --run outputs\intervention --baseline outputs\main
.\.venv\Scripts\python src\figures.py --run outputs\main --intervention outputs\intervention
.\.venv\Scripts\python report\build_report.py                                              # report.md, defense.md, README.md
.\.venv\Scripts\python report\make_slides.py                                               # presentation.pptx, speaker_notes.md
```
Generation and attention extraction skip work already on disk; run only one generation process per output folder. Outputs: `outputs/main/{{images,samples.jsonl,detections.jsonl,eval.jsonl,attention,results,figures}}`, `outputs/intervention/{{images,results}}`.

## Remaining limitations
4-6 prompts per category with different objects; low base rates (floor effects); evaluator errors and one non-independent annotator; spatial barely validated; size attributes not evaluated; one model, scheduler and resolution; coarse CFG grid;
attention analyses are correlational and exploratory; the intervention was tested at one CFG, one step count and one token-selection rule; no confirmation set for the exploratory presence result.
